explanation_html: The app uses computer vision to identify the specific painting from the camera feed, then triggers the corresponding audio description.

question_html: In a speech-to-speech translation system, why might the translator omit “ums” and “uhs”?

options.text: To produce a more fluent and cleaner output
Because they contain crucial semantic meaning

explanation_html: Disfluency removal is a common preprocessing step to make the translation sound more natural and professional.

question_html: What is the output of an “image super-resolution” model?

options.text: A lower-resolution version of the input
A higher-resolution image with finer details inferred
A text description of the image

explanation_html: Super-resolution upscales an image, using AI to hallucinate plausible high-frequency details missing from the low-res input.

question_html: In document AI, what does “signature detection” accomplish?

options.text: Locating the presence and area of a signature on a document
Converting a signature to a digital certificate

explanation_html: Signature detection identifies if and where a signature is present, often used to confirm a document was signed without analyzing the signature itself.

question_html: Which of the following is a typical use case for a multimodal large language model in media?

options.text: Answering questions about a video by watching and listening to it

explanation_html: Multimodal LLMs can process video, audio, and text simultaneously, allowing a user to ask, “What did the person say about the budget?” and get an answer.

question_html: In automatic speech recognition, what does the “acoustic model” map?

options.text: Audio features to phonemes or linguistic units

explanation_html: The acoustic model takes acoustic features and predicts the probability of phonemes or subword units.

question_html: What is the function of a “pooling layer” in a CNN?

options.text: To increase the number of channels
To progressively reduce the spatial dimensions and summarize features

explanation_html: Pooling (max or average) reduces resolution, making the representation more compact and invariant to small translations.

question_html: In a multimodal assistant, the system correctly understands “play the song with the beach music video” and starts the song. Which capability is essential?

options.text: Entity linking between textual query and a multimedia database

explanation_html: The assistant must link the natural language request to a specific media asset by matching metadata and possibly visual content understanding.

question_html: What is the purpose of “token merging” in some vision transformers?

options.text: To increase the number of patches
To combine redundant image patches to reduce computation
To convert image tokens to text tokens

explanation_html: Token merging accelerates ViT inference by gradually merging similar tokens, maintaining accuracy while reducing computational load.

question_html: In speech technology, what is “keyword spotting”?

options.text: Detecting predefined words or phrases like "Hey Siri" within an audio stream
Translating a single keyword into multiple languages

explanation_html: Keyword spotting (or wake word detection) is an always-on lightweight system to trigger a full ASR pipeline.

question_html: What is the purpose of “image augmentation” techniques like random cropping and flipping?

options.text: To simulate variations and prevent overfitting
To permanently alter the original files

explanation_html: Augmentation exposes the model to a wider range of inputs, improving its ability to generalize to unseen data.

question_html: In document intelligence, what is “line item extraction” commonly used for?

options.text: Extracting the header of a document
Pulling out individual rows of products or services from an invoice
Formatting the font of the line

explanation_html: Line item extraction identifies and structures each row in an invoice, capturing description, quantity, unit price, and total.

question_html: A video analytics system can count how many people cross a line. What is this task called?

options.text: People counting with line crossing detection

explanation_html: This uses object detection and tracking to increment a counter when a person’s trajectory crosses a virtual line.

question_html: In audio signal processing, what does “sampling rate” define?

options.text: The number of audio samples per second
The bit depth of each sample

explanation_html: Sampling rate (e.g., 16 kHz) determines the temporal resolution of the digital audio signal, directly affecting frequency bandwidth.

question_html: What is a “visual grounding” task?

options.text: Classifying an image into a category
Locating an object in an image based on a natural language description
Converting an image to a sketch

explanation_html: Visual grounding (or referring expression comprehension) links words to image regions, localizing “the red car next to the tree.”

question_html: Which of the following is an example of using AI for media accessibility?

options.text: Using facial recognition to unlock a phone
Automatically generating sign language avatars from spoken news

explanation_html: Converting speech or text to sign language is a direct accessibility application, making content available to deaf or hard-of-hearing users.

question_html: In a neural machine translation system, what does “beam search” do during decoding?

options.text: Keeps multiple candidate sequences to find a translation with higher overall score

explanation_html: Beam search explores several partial hypotheses in parallel to avoid greedy mistakes and find more fluent outputs.

question_html: What is a “confusion matrix” used for in evaluating an image classifier?

options.text: Showing the number of correct and incorrect predictions per class
Plotting the loss curve over epochs

explanation_html: A confusion matrix breaks down true positives, false positives, etc., for each class, helping identify where the model confuses categories.

question_html: In a multimodal model that generates images from text, what is the typical role of a text encoder?

options.text: Converting the text prompt into a latent representation that conditions the image generation process
Decoding the image into a caption

explanation_html: The text encoder (often a transformer) embeds the prompt into a vector that guides the generative model to produce a matching image.

question_html: What does “endpoint detection” do in a voice assistant?

options.text: Determines when the user has finished speaking

explanation_html: Endpoint detection (or end-of-speech detection) signals the system to stop recording and process the utterance, crucial for smooth interaction.

question_html: Which AI technique is used to remove watermarks or logos from videos in an automated way?
explanation_html: Video inpainting fills in the region of the watermark with plausible background content by analyzing surrounding frames.

question_html: In document AI, “handprinted” text recognition refers to:

options.text: Recognizing discrete, machine-like characters written by hand

explanation_html: Handprinted text is written character by character (like on a form) and is generally easier to recognize than fully cursive handwriting.

question_html: What does “fine-tuning a large language model with multimodal data” enable?

options.text: The model can only answer text questions
The model learns to relate visual concepts with language for tasks like image captioning or VQA
The model requires more time to process text
The model becomes a speech synthesizer

explanation_html: Adding multimodal data during fine-tuning aligns vision and language representations, unlocking cross-modal understanding.

question_html: In a voice-controlled drone, which AI capability is essential for understanding commands like “follow the red car”?

options.text: Speech recognition and visual object tracking

explanation_html: The drone must transcribe the spoken command and use computer vision to identify and track the specified target.

question_html: What does “text-to-image alignment score” measure?

options.text: The resolution of the generated image
How well a generated image corresponds to the input text prompt
The file size of the image

explanation_html: Using models like CLIP, the alignment score quantifies semantic similarity between prompt and generated image.

question_html: Which of the following is a concern when deploying facial recognition in public spaces?

options.text: Privacy and ethical implications regarding mass surveillance and bias
It does not require a camera

explanation_html: Responsible AI practices require addressing bias, consent, and privacy when using facial recognition, especially in public.

question_html: What is a “diffusion model” for audio generation?

options.text: A generative model that gradually denoises random noise into structured audio based on a prompt
A model that classifies audio events

explanation_html: Diffusion models for audio synthesize high-fidelity music or speech by reversing a noise process, similar to image diffusion.

question_html: In computer vision, what is “few-shot object detection”?

options.text: Training a detector to recognize a new object class with only a few examples
Detecting millions of objects at once
Using a single large model for all tasks

explanation_html: Few-shot detection adapts quickly to new categories using limited labeled images, often by leveraging a well-pretrained backbone.

question_html: A podcast platform wants to recommend episodes based on a transcript snippet that a user liked. Which technology matches the snippet to similar episodes?
explanation_html: The snippet is embedded, and the system retrieves episodes with similar vector representations, enabling content-based recommendation.

question_html: In speech recognition, what does “domain adaptation” help with?

options.text: Making the model work only for one domain
Improving accuracy on specialized vocabulary (e.g., medical terms) by fine-tuning on in-domain data

explanation_html: Domain adaptation tailors a general ASR model to the jargon, acronyms, and speaking style of a specific industry.

question_html: What does “grounding” mean in the context of multimodal LLMs?

options.text: Connecting generated text to specific parts of the input (e.g., citing an image region or a document passage)
Training the model on the ground
Removing the context from the output

explanation_html: Grounding ensures the model’s answer can be traced back to evidence in the provided visual or textual input, reducing hallucination.

question_html: Which of these is a typical application of “gesture recognition” in media systems?

options.text: Allowing a user to control a smart TV by waving their hand

explanation_html: Camera-based gesture recognition interprets human hand and body motions as commands, enabling touchless interaction.

question_html: In a text-to-speech model, “attention alignment” during training ensures:

options.text: The model learns to attend to the correct input tokens when generating each output acoustic frame

explanation_html: TTS models use attention to align text tokens with speech frames; accurate alignment is critical for intelligible synthesis.

question_html: What is a “data augmentation” technique specific to audio?

options.text: Adding background noise, changing speed, or applying pitch shift

explanation_html: Augmenting audio with variations in tempo, pitch, and additive noise improves model robustness for ASR and audio classification.

question_html: In multimodal content moderation, why is analyzing both audio and visual streams important?

options.text: Some policy violations might only be detectable in one modality (e.g., hate speech in audio, violence in video)
It reduces the need for any human review

explanation_html: Combining modalities catches a wider range of harmful content that might be missed if only one signal is checked.

question_html: Which metric is used for evaluating image captioning?
explanation_html: Image captioning evaluation uses metrics like BLEU, METEOR, or CIDEr that compare generated captions to human references.

question_html: In a legal tech company, AI reviews contracts to flag risky clauses. What type of document intelligence is this?
explanation_html: This involves NLP and structured extraction to identify and categorize contractual clauses, a specialized document understanding task.

question_html: What is a “multi-talker ASR” system designed to handle?

options.text: A single speaker reading a script
Overlapping speech from multiple people (e.g., a meeting with cross-talk)

explanation_html: Multi-talker or overlapping speech recognition separates and transcribes simultaneous speakers, a very challenging area.

question_html: In a multimodal AI system for retail, what does “shelf analysis” involve?

options.text: Using computer vision to identify products, check stock levels, and verify planogram compliance

explanation_html: Shelf analysis uses object detection and classification on photos of shelves to monitor inventory and layout.

question_html: What is the function of a “phoneme” in speech technology?

options.text: The smallest perceptually distinct unit of sound in a language

explanation_html: Phonemes are the building blocks of pronunciation; “cat” has three phonemes: /k/, /æ/, /t/.

question_html: Which of the following is an example of “intelligent document redaction”?

options.text: Automatically locating and obscuring personally identifiable information (PII) like social security numbers

explanation_html: AI can detect sensitive entities and apply black boxes or removal to ensure privacy compliance before sharing.

question_html: In a voice cloning system, what is “zero-shot voice cloning”?

options.text: Cloning a voice from thousands of hours of data
Generating speech in a target voice using only a few seconds of reference audio, without specific training on that speaker
Cloning a voice without any audio at all
Removing a voice from an audio track

explanation_html: Zero-shot TTS models can instantly mimic a new speaker’s voice from a short sample by leveraging speaker embeddings.

question_html: What does “image captioning with dense annotations” add over a single caption?

options.text: Detailed descriptions of multiple regions and objects in the image

explanation_html: Dense captioning locates and describes several regions in an image, providing a richer understanding of the full scene.

question_html: In ASR, what is a “confidence filter” used for?

options.text: To discard low-certainty recognition results, often routing them for human review

explanation_html: A confidence threshold helps balance automation and accuracy; low-confidence transcriptions can be flagged for manual correction.

question_html: Which of the following best describes the concept of “foundation models for media intelligence”?

options.text: Small, specialized models trained for a single format
Large, pre-trained AI models that can be adapted to various media-related tasks across modalities
Models that only process raw text files
Database systems for storing media assets

explanation_html: Foundation models, like multimodal LLMs, serve as a versatile base that can be fine-tuned or prompted for diverse media analysis, generation, and understanding tasks.

question_html: Which metric is most appropriate for measuring the proportion of actual positive cases correctly identified by a binary classification model in a security threat detection system?
explanation_html: Recall (also called sensitivity) measures the proportion of actual positives that are correctly identified. In security threat detection, missing a real threat (false negative) is highly dangerous, so a high recall is prioritized to catch as many threats as possible. Precision would focus on reducing false alarms, but recall directly addresses the need to detect all true threats.

question_html: An organization deploys an AI chatbot. After three months, users report that the bot frequently gives offensive replies to certain prompts. Which responsible AI principle is most directly violated?
explanation_html: Safety in responsible AI means the system should avoid generating harmful or offensive content. Offensive replies pose a direct risk to user well-being and trust. Fairness relates to bias and equal treatment, transparency to explainability, and accountability to ownership of outcomes, but the immediate issue here is content safety.

question_html: What is the primary purpose of an AI content safety filter in a production generative AI application?

options.text: To block or flag harmful inputs and outputs

explanation_html: A content safety filter monitors prompts and model responses to detect and mitigate harmful content such as hate speech, violence, or illegal material. It helps maintain compliance with responsible AI policies. It does not directly affect speed, data anonymization, or token compression.

question_html: During a security review, the team discovers that an attacker can extract sensitive training data by submitting carefully crafted queries to a deployed LLM. Which type of attack is this?
explanation_html: Model inversion attacks aim to reconstruct private training data by querying the model and analyzing its outputs. Prompt injection involves manipulating the model’s behavior through input, not extracting data. Data poisoning happens during training, and denial of service targets availability. Model inversion is a known privacy threat.

question_html: In an MLOps pipeline, which practice helps ensure that a new model version does not introduce bias before production deployment?

options.text: Fairness evaluation on a holdout dataset

explanation_html: Fairness evaluation on a representative holdout dataset checks for disparate impact across different groups before deployment. A/B testing occurs after deployment, increasing epochs doesn’t guarantee bias reduction, and rate limiting is an operational control. Pre-deployment fairness checks are essential for responsible AI governance.

question_html: A production model’s accuracy drops significantly over two weeks. Which monitoring technique would first alert you to a possible data drift?

options.text: Comparing input feature distributions against a training baseline
Running unit tests on model code

explanation_html: Data drift detection involves comparing statistical properties of current input data with those of the training data. A significant shift in feature distributions signals that the model may be encountering different patterns, leading to performance decay. CPU usage and login logs are unrelated, and unit tests verify code logic, not data quality.

question_html: Which of the following is a core requirement of the EU AI Act for high-risk AI systems regarding transparency?

options.text: Users must be informed when interacting with an AI system
Training data must be publicly shared
All model parameters must be published

explanation_html: The EU AI Act mandates that individuals be informed when they are interacting with an AI system, especially for high-risk applications. This transparency obligation ensures users are aware they are not dealing with a human. Open-sourcing or publishing parameters is not a universal legal requirement.

question_html: A team uses a canary deployment strategy for a new recommendation model. What is the primary benefit of this approach?

options.text: It eliminates the need for monitoring
It limits the blast radius by routing a small fraction of traffic to the new model
It instantly retrains the model if errors occur

explanation_html: Canary deployment sends a small percentage of production traffic to the new model version to observe its behavior and performance. If issues arise, only a limited user base is affected, minimizing risk. It still requires monitoring and does not inherently cut costs or auto-retrain.

question_html: In a responsible AI governance framework, which team typically owns the definition and enforcement of AI ethics principles across projects?

options.text: AI ethics board or review committee

explanation_html: An AI ethics board or cross-functional review committee sets organization-wide ethical guidelines, reviews high-risk use cases, and ensures compliance with principles like fairness and transparency. Operations and engineering teams implement controls, but the governance body defines policy.

question_html: What is the purpose of an error budget in an AI service’s reliability strategy?

options.text: To allocate funds for model retraining
To define the acceptable amount of unreliability before changes are frozen
To measure the carbon footprint of inference
To calculate the cost per prediction

explanation_html: An error budget is the maximum allowed deviation from service level objectives (SLOs) over a time window. When the budget is exhausted, teams prioritize reliability improvements over new feature releases. It is a core concept of site reliability engineering applied to AI systems.

question_html: Which technique helps an image classification model distinguish between a wolf and a husky by learning to focus on the background (snow) rather than the animal?

options.text: Adversarial training to reduce spurious correlations
Adding more wolf images without snow

explanation_html: Techniques like adversarial debiasing force the model to rely on the animal’s features rather than confounding background context.

question_html: In a factory, a visual inspection system flags scratched parts. What type of training data is used?

options.text: Images of parts labeled as "defective" or "ok"

explanation_html: A computer vision defect detection model learns from labeled image examples to distinguish good parts from those with anomalies.

question_html: What is “prosody transfer” in speech synthesis?

options.text: Applying the intonation and rhythm pattern from one utterance to another

explanation_html: Prosody transfer allows a synthetic voice to adopt the speaking style of a reference audio, making it more expressive.

question_html: In document AI, what is the role of “prebuilt models” in cloud services?

options.text: They require training from scratch for every document
They provide ready-to-use extraction for common document types like invoices and receipts
They only work for handwritten text

explanation_html: Prebuilt models are trained on large datasets of standard business documents, offering instant data extraction with high accuracy.

question_html: A multimodal AI system can “hallucinate.” What does this mean?

options.text: It generates plausible but factually incorrect or non-existent content
It works only during the night
It uses computer vision for mental health

explanation_html: Hallucination refers to the model confidently making up details not present in the input, a known challenge in generative AI.

question_html: In ASR, what is an “n-gram language model” used for?

options.text: To estimate the probability of a word sequence based on the previous few words

explanation_html: An n-gram LM helps the ASR decoder choose more probable word sequences, improving transcription accuracy.

question_html: Which of these is a typical use of facial analysis in an event photography platform?

options.text: Grouping photos by person using face clustering

explanation_html: Face clustering organizes a large collection of photos by detected identities, making it easy for attendees to find their pictures.

question_html: In a “text-to-image” system, what does the “diffusion process” do?

options.text: Gradually removes noise from a random image guided by the text prompt

explanation_html: Diffusion models learn to reverse a noising process, generating high-quality images conditioned on text embeddings.

question_html: What is the primary benefit of “real-time captioning” using AI during live events?

options.text: It reduces the need for speakers
It provides immediate accessibility for deaf and hard-of-hearing attendees
It translates the event into sign language

explanation_html: Live captioning converts speech to text on the fly, making presentations inclusive for those who cannot hear the audio.

question_html: In audio event detection, what is a “soundscape”?

options.text: The complete acoustic environment with multiple simultaneous sound sources

explanation_html: Soundscape analysis aims to identify and describe all audible events in a recording, such as traffic, birds, and voices together.

question_html: Which of the following is a challenge in OCR for historical documents?

options.text: Degraded paper, variable handwriting, and outdated typography

explanation_html: Historical documents present difficulties like faded ink, bleed-through, and irregular letter shapes that challenge standard OCR.

question_html: In a multimodal model, what does “modality dropout” during training aim to achieve?

options.text: Forcing the model to rely on any single modality, improving robustness when one modality is missing at inference

explanation_html: Randomly dropping a modality during training encourages the model to learn from each independently and not overfit to a specific combination.

question_html: A security system uses “voice biometrics.” What is it comparing?

options.text: Unique physical and behavioral vocal characteristics of the speaker

explanation_html: Voice biometrics analyzes the speaker’s voiceprint—features like pitch, cadence, and vocal tract shape—not the words themselves.

question_html: What does “semantic search” over a media library allow a user to do?

options.text: Search using only exact file names
Find content by describing it in natural language, e.g., "scenes with a red car at sunset"

explanation_html: Multimodal embeddings enable searching images and videos using textual descriptions without manual tags.

question_html: In a call transcription tool, the output includes “Speaker 1: … Speaker 2: …”. This is a result of:
explanation_html: Diarization separates the audio into homogeneous segments according to speaker identity and labels them.

question_html: Which of the following best describes a “vision encoder” in a multimodal LLM?

options.text: A module that generates text captions
A neural network that converts an image into a sequence of feature vectors
A component that converts speech to text

explanation_html: The vision encoder (e.g., ViT) transforms the raw image into embeddings that can be interleaved with text tokens for joint processing.

question_html: In generative AI for media, what is “style transfer”?

options.text: Applying the artistic style of one image to the content of another
Detecting the font of a text

explanation_html: Neural style transfer separates and recombines content and style representations, creating a new image with the content of one and the style of another.

question_html: What is the purpose of “phoneme alignment” in a TTS dataset?

options.text: To label each audio frame with the corresponding phoneme
To separate voice from background music
To increase the volume of the audio

explanation_html: Accurate time-aligned phoneme labels are essential for training duration models and improving TTS naturalness.

question_html: A video conferencing app offers an “AI summary” of the meeting. What modalities are used?

options.text: Audio transcript and screen share OCR, possibly combined

explanation_html: Modern meeting summaries combine the spoken transcript with any text presented on screen to capture the full context.

question_html: In computer vision, what is “optical character verification” (OCV)?

options.text: Detecting if text is present in an image
Checking that a known string (e.g., a date code) is printed correctly and legibly

explanation_html: OCV is used in manufacturing to validate printed labels, ensuring the correct characters are present and of acceptable quality.

question_html: Which of the following is a benefit of “multitask learning” in a speech model?

options.text: The model can only do one thing well
A single model trained jointly on ASR, translation, and language ID can share knowledge and improve each task
It requires separate models for each task

explanation_html: Multitask training leverages common representations, often leading to better generalization than training each task independently.

question_html: In multimodal AI, what does “early exit” or “anytime prediction” refer to?

options.text: Dynamically deciding to output a prediction from an intermediate layer to save computation for easy inputs

explanation_html: Adaptive computation allows models to respond faster when confident, reducing latency in real-time applications.

question_html: A retail analytics system counts foot traffic and estimates customer demographics. Which AI task provides the age and gender estimates?
explanation_html: Face attribute models predict demographic labels from facial appearance, while preserving privacy by not identifying the individual.

question_html: In speech processing, what does “source separation” aim to do?

options.text: Identify the language of a speaker
Isolate individual sound sources from a mixture (e.g., separate two speakers or voice from music)

explanation_html: Source separation (cocktail party problem) extracts clean signals for each source, improving downstream tasks.

question_html: What is a “vector database” used for in a multimodal search system?

options.text: Efficiently indexing and querying high-dimensional embeddings

explanation_html: Embeddings of images, text, or audio are stored in a vector database, allowing fast similarity search for retrieval applications.

question_html: In document processing, what does “form understanding” provide beyond simple OCR?

options.text: Structured extraction of fields like name, address, and checkboxes with their labels
A spoken read-out of the form

explanation_html: Form understanding models map text and spatial layout to a predefined schema, turning unstructured forms into structured data.

question_html: Which of the following is a key advantage of “on-device” speech recognition over cloud-based ASR?

options.text: Lower latency and privacy (no data leaves the device)

explanation_html: On-device processing keeps user data local and works without internet, but often uses smaller, optimized models.

question_html: In a video surveillance system, “anomaly detection” might flag:

options.text: Unusual events like a person running in a typically quiet hallway

explanation_html: Anomaly detection learns patterns of normal activity and raises alerts for deviations, useful for security.

question_html: What is “text-to-speech with emotion”?

options.text: Synthesizing speech with a specified emotional tone, like happy or sad

explanation_html: Emotional TTS controls prosody and voice quality to convey feelings, making interactions more natural and engaging.

question_html: In a multimodal chatbot, how can the model “see” an image if it’s a language-only LLM adapted for vision?

options.text: By using a vision encoder to project the image into the model's token embedding space
By converting the image to ASCII art
By describing the image with rules

explanation_html: A visual projection layer maps image features into a sequence of embeddings that the LLM can process as if they were words.

question_html: An organization wants to ensure that only models approved by the risk committee are deployed to production. Which practice enforces this?

options.text: A gated CI/CD pipeline with automated policy checks and approval steps
Storing models in a shared folder

explanation_html: A gated pipeline can enforce that a model passes automated tests (e.g., bias, security) and receives required human approvals before deployment. This embeds governance into the workflow.

question_html: When deploying a model behind an API, which HTTP status code family generally indicates a client-side error such as a malformed request?
explanation_html: 4xx status codes (like 400 Bad Request, 401 Unauthorized) mean the request is invalid or unauthorized. 5xx indicates server-side issues. Proper error handling is part of operational robustness.

question_html: A company uses differential privacy when training a model on sensitive user data. What is the main goal?

options.text: To provide a mathematical guarantee that individual data points cannot be inferred from the model

explanation_html: Differential privacy adds calibrated noise to obscure the contribution of any single record, bounding the risk of re-identification. It does not primarily aim to improve accuracy or speed.

question_html: Which metric is most appropriate for evaluating a multi-class image classifier’s overall performance when classes are imbalanced?
explanation_html: Macro-averaged F1 calculates the F1-score for each class independently and then averages, giving equal weight to minority classes, making it more informative than accuracy for imbalanced data.

question_html: In a production AI environment, what is the function of a circuit breaker pattern?

options.text: To stop sending requests to a failing service to prevent cascading failures

explanation_html: A circuit breaker detects when a downstream service is failing and opens the circuit, fast-failing requests for a period to allow recovery, thereby maintaining overall system stability.

question_html: A MLOps engineer needs to ensure that the pre-processing logic applied to inference requests exactly matches that used during training. Which tooling component helps enforce this consistency?

options.text: A feature engineering pipeline defined as code and versioned

explanation_html: Defining feature transformations as versioned code (pipeline-as-code) and using a feature store or shared library guarantees that the same transformations are applied in both training and serving, preventing skew. A model registry stores model versions, but doesn’t enforce feature consistency.

question_html: What does the principle of “explainability” require from a high-risk AI system?

options.text: The model must be 100% accurate for all decisions
The system’s decisions and the underlying logic must be understandable to stakeholders
All training data must be publicly released

explanation_html: Explainability means that humans can comprehend how and why an AI model arrived at a particular output. It’s crucial for trust, debugging, and regulatory compliance. It does not demand perfect accuracy, data publication, or uptime.

question_html: In a cloud environment, an AI model artifact is stored in blob storage. What is a key security control to prevent unauthorized access?

options.text: Using public read access for all containers
Enforcing identity-based access policies and encryption at rest
Embedding the access key in the application code

explanation_html: Access policies (IAM) and encryption ensure that only authorized services or users can read or modify the model files. Public access and embedded keys are security risks, and disabling logging hurts auditing.

question_html: A team notices that model performance degrades every Monday morning but recovers later in the week. What type of drift might this indicate?

options.text: Cyclical or recurring drift due to weekly pattern changes in data
Model staleness that only appears on Mondays

explanation_html: Performance fluctuations tied to day-of-week patterns suggest cyclical changes in user behavior or data distribution. This is a recurring drift that may require incorporating temporal features. Permanent drift would not recover, and it’s not an attack.

question_html: Which of the following is an example of operational excellence in AI lifecycle management?

options.text: Automating model retraining pipelines triggered by performance degradation alerts
Using only manual code reviews for model validation
Running a single test environment for all stages

explanation_html: Automated retraining pipelines that respond to monitoring alerts reduce manual toil and accelerate recovery from drift, embodying operational excellence. Lack of monitoring, manual-only validation, and single environment are anti-patterns.

question_html: A user reports that an AI recommendation system always suggests the same few items regardless of their behavior. This suggests what kind of problem?

options.text: Feedback loop leading to filter bubble

explanation_html: A filter bubble or over-reinforcement of popular items can happen when the model’s recommendations are fed back into its own training or inference loop, reducing diversity. It’s a feedback loop effect, not a drift or latency issue.

question_html: When evaluating a generative AI model for code generation, which metric would assess how often the generated code passes a set of unit tests?
explanation_html: Pass@k measures the probability that at least one of k generated code samples passes the given tests, a standard metric for code generation quality. BLEU and perplexity are for natural language, recall for classification.

question_html: What is the primary purpose of a data provenance tracking system in responsible AI?

options.text: To record the origin, transformations, and usage rights of data used in AI models

explanation_html: Data provenance (lineage) documentation ensures that data sources, consent, and processing steps are transparent, aiding compliance with regulations and enabling auditing. It doesn’t compress, speed up training, or cache predictions.

question_html: In the context of AI threat modeling, what does “model theft” refer to?

options.text: Unauthorized copying or extraction of a trained model’s functionality or parameters

explanation_html: Model theft is an attack where an adversary extracts enough information to replicate a proprietary model, often via API querying. It undermines intellectual property and competitive advantage. Physical theft and accidental deletion are different concerns.

question_html: A customer service chatbot uses a knowledge base. Which operational metric best indicates the proportion of queries successfully resolved without human escalation?
explanation_html: Self-service resolution rate measures how many customer issues are completely resolved by the AI without needing a human agent. Handoff rate is the opposite. Response time and API call count don’t measure resolution effectiveness.

question_html: What is the primary objective of conducting regular red-teaming exercises on an AI system?

options.text: To test the model’s accuracy on a validation set
To find security and safety weaknesses through adversarial simulation
To evaluate the energy consumption of training
To measure the model’s learning rate convergence

explanation_html: Red-teaming involves experts deliberately trying to make the model fail or produce harmful outputs, uncovering vulnerabilities that standard evaluation might miss, thus strengthening safety and security.

question_html: Which of the following is an example of a process that supports continuous monitoring of responsible AI metrics in production?

options.text: Automated daily fairness metric dashboards with alerts
Running a one-time fairness check before launch

explanation_html: Continuous monitoring requires automated, ongoing measurement with alerts, not just periodic or pre-launch checks. This ensures timely detection of fairness deviations in production.

question_html: In a cloud-based AI service, what is the main purpose of auto-scaling inference endpoints?

options.text: To dynamically adjust the number of server instances based on request load
To retrain the model on new data

explanation_html: Auto-scaling ensures that the service can handle variable traffic by adding or removing instances, maintaining performance and cost efficiency. It does not impact model accuracy or features.

question_html: A model’s API logs contain personally identifiable information (PII) in the request payloads. What is the most critical action to take?

options.text: Archive the logs permanently for debugging
Implement log scrubbing or masking to remove PII immediately
Send logs to a public cloud storage

explanation_html: Storing PII in logs violates privacy regulations and increases breach risk. Log scrubbing (redaction) removes or masks sensitive data before storage, while still allowing useful debugging information.

question_html: What does “ground truth” refer to in model evaluation?

options.text: The verified, correct labels or outcomes used as a reference

explanation_html: Ground truth is the actual, accurate data used to compare against model predictions to calculate performance metrics. It can be human-labeled or derived from trusted sources.

question_html: A team discovers that a deployed model was trained on data containing unlicensed copyrighted material. Which responsible AI pillar does this breach most directly?
explanation_html: Using unlicensed data violates legal and ethical standards around intellectual property, falling under accountability and compliance. The team must ensure data usage aligns with legal agreements and responsible sourcing.

question_html: When using a blue/green deployment strategy for an AI service, what does the “green” environment represent?

options.text: The production environment currently serving users
The idle environment with the new version being validated

explanation_html: In blue/green deployment, blue is the live production environment, and green is a fully staged environment with the new version. After testing, traffic is switched to green, enabling zero-downtime deployment and easy rollback.

question_html: A responsible AI audit typically examines which of the following?

options.text: Documentation, fairness assessments, privacy safeguards, and governance processes
The color scheme of the UI

explanation_html: AI audits review the entire system’s alignment with ethical, legal, and policy requirements, including data governance, bias testing, transparency documentation, and ongoing monitoring practices.

question_html: What is the key benefit of using a canary analysis tool like an automated rollback based on key metrics?

options.text: It reduces the need for any human supervision
It automatically detects regressions during a canary deployment and rolls back if metrics degrade
It retrains the model with zero data

explanation_html: Canary analysis tools compare the performance of the canary instance against a baseline using statistical tests and can trigger an automatic rollback if significant degradation is detected, reducing mean time to recovery.

question_html: A language translation model shows excellent BLEU scores on test sets but poor user satisfaction in production. What is the most likely reason?

options.text: The test set covers all possible user inputs
Automatic metrics may not fully capture semantic adequacy and fluency perceived by humans
The model was trained too recently

explanation_html: BLEU measures n-gram overlap and can miss meaning, fluency, or context errors. Human evaluation often reveals quality gaps that automatic metrics overlook, leading to a discrepancy.

question_html: In an AI system, what is the purpose of maintaining an audit trail of all model predictions and associated metadata?

options.text: To support post-hoc investigation, compliance, and debugging

explanation_html: Audit trails log who, what, and when for each prediction, enabling forensic analysis, regulatory audits, and identifying patterns of failure or bias. They do not affect speed or memory directly.

question_html: What does “model distillation” refer to in a production context?

options.text: Compressing a large model into a smaller, faster one with similar performance
Splitting the model across multiple GPUs

explanation_html: Distillation trains a compact student model to mimic a large teacher model, reducing latency and resource usage while preserving accuracy, often used for edge deployment.

question_html: Which principle dictates that AI systems should be designed so that their failure modes can be anticipated and managed safely?
explanation_html: Safety and robustness require that systems are engineered to avoid harm, including understanding potential failure modes and mitigating their impact. It’s a fundamental responsible AI tenet.

question_html: A model monitoring system triggers an alert when the proportion of empty input fields exceeds 5%. This alert is an example of monitoring for what?
explanation_html: Empty or missing input fields indicate a data quality problem, possibly from a faulty upstream data source. Monitoring such data integrity checks is essential for reliable AI operations.

question_html: In an inference pipeline, a retry mechanism with exponential backoff is primarily used to handle which type of error?

options.text: Transient errors due to temporary network or service issues (5xx, timeouts)
Malformed input that will never succeed

explanation_html: Exponential backoff retries are suitable for transient failures where the issue may resolve after a short delay, like a momentary network blip or server overload. Retrying on client errors (4xx) is usually pointless.

question_html: A financial services AI model denies loan applications. The regulator requires evidence that the model does not discriminate based on protected attributes. Which evaluation method is most appropriate?

options.text: Group fairness metrics like demographic parity difference

explanation_html: Group fairness metrics quantify differences in outcomes across demographic groups, directly measuring discrimination. Cross-validation assesses generalizability, F1-score measures overall performance, and latency is irrelevant to fairness.

question_html: When evaluating a model for deployment, what does a confusion matrix primarily help you understand?

options.text: The distribution of prediction errors across classes

explanation_html: A confusion matrix tabulates true positives, false positives, true negatives, and false negatives for classification problems, showing exactly which classes are confused with each other. It provides detailed insight into error patterns beyond a single metric.

question_html: An AI system’s outputs systematically disadvantage a specific demographic group. Which type of harm does this represent?
explanation_html: Unfair bias causing systematic disadvantage to a group is a fairness-related harm, often categorized as allocative (denial of resources/opportunities) or representational. Privacy violations involve data exposure, model extraction is theft, and latency degradation is a performance issue.

question_html: Which document provides a structured way to communicate an AI model’s intended use, performance characteristics, and limitations to end users and regulators?
explanation_html: Model cards (or system cards) are transparency artifacts that describe the model’s context, evaluation results, and ethical considerations. They help meet responsible AI disclosure requirements. SLAs define uptime guarantees, API specs describe technical interfaces, and code docs are for developers.

question_html: In production operations, what is the primary role of observability in an AI system?

options.text: To enable understanding of system internal state from external outputs

explanation_html: Observability provides insights into a system’s health and behavior through metrics, logs, and traces, allowing teams to diagnose issues without deploying new code. It’s crucial for monitoring and troubleshooting AI services, not for training speed or encryption.

question_html: A company must comply with GDPR when processing personal data with an AI model. Which of the following is a required capability under GDPR?

options.text: Users have the right to request deletion of their data from training sets
All decisions must be made solely by automated processing
Model weights must be stored on EU servers only

explanation_html: GDPR grants data subjects the right to erasure (“right to be forgotten”), which extends to deleting personal data used in AI training when applicable. Accuracy is not a legal requirement, automated decision-making has restrictions, and while data residency is relevant, the deletion right is a core obligation.

question_html: What is the main advantage of using shadow deployment when rolling out a new model version?

options.text: It allows the new model to process production traffic alongside the old model without affecting users
It automatically labels new training data

explanation_html: In shadow deployment, the new model receives a copy of live traffic and its outputs are logged and compared, but not served to users. This enables realistic testing without user impact. It does not eliminate downtime by itself, nor auto-label data.

question_html: Which of the following is a common key performance indicator (KPI) for monitoring an AI API’s operational health?

options.text: Number of likes on social media

explanation_html: Latency, especially high percentiles like P99, reflects the worst-case response times users experience and is critical for SLO monitoring. Social media likes, code changes, and parameter count are not operational health metrics.

question_html: What is the main goal of adversarial testing in AI security?

options.text: To identify vulnerabilities by simulating malicious inputs
To compress the model for mobile deployment

explanation_html: Adversarial testing crafts inputs designed to cause misclassification or unsafe outputs, revealing weaknesses in model robustness. It is a proactive security measure. It does not measure emissions, compress models, or generate data for training.

question_html: In a Responsible AI lifecycle, when should a human review process be incorporated for high-risk decisions?

options.text: Only after a legal complaint is filed
Throughout the design, deployment, and monitoring phases
Never, because AI must be fully autonomous

explanation_html: Human oversight should be embedded from design through ongoing monitoring for high-stakes AI systems, as required by regulations like the EU AI Act. This ensures accountability and the ability to intervene when the model errs.

question_html: A team observes that the distribution of input text lengths in production has shifted significantly from the training data. What is this phenomenon called?
explanation_html: Feature drift, or data drift, occurs when the statistical properties of input features change. A shift in text length distribution is a classic example. Concept drift refers to changes in the relationship between inputs and target, label drift to changes in output distribution, and model staleness is a general term.

question_html: Which technique can help mitigate bias in a classification model during training?

options.text: Adding more layers to the neural network

explanation_html: Fairness-aware algorithms can incorporate constraints or re-weight training instances to reduce disparate impact. Architectural changes (more layers) or hardware changes do not address bias directly, and batch size affects training dynamics, not fairness.

question_html: When evaluating a text summarization model, which metric focuses on the overlap of n-grams between the generated summary and a reference summary?
explanation_html: ROUGE (Recall-Oriented Understudy for Gisting Evaluation) measures n-gram overlap, particularly recall, between generated and reference texts. BLEU is more common for machine translation, perplexity evaluates language model confidence, and MOS is subjective human scoring.

question_html: An incident response plan for AI systems should include a procedure for rolling back a model when what occurs?

options.text: The model’s accuracy is above the target
A critical security vulnerability or severe performance degradation is detected

explanation_html: A rollback procedure is part of incident management to quickly revert to a previous stable version if a new model introduces security flaws or unacceptable performance, minimizing user impact.

question_html: What is the function of a gatekeeper model in a responsible AI architecture?

options.text: To act as an additional layer that reviews and filters outputs for policy violations
To balance load across inference servers
To compress the model before serving

explanation_html: A gatekeeper (or guard) model sits alongside the main AI model to check outputs for toxicity, PII leakage, or other policy violations, blocking or rewriting them if necessary. This adds a safety net beyond built-in safeguards.

question_html: Which method helps protect a deployed LLM from prompt injection attacks that try to bypass system instructions?

options.text: Input sanitization and pre-processing with guardrails

explanation_html: Input sanitization and guardrails inspect and clean user inputs to remove or neutralize malicious patterns before they reach the model. This is a key defense against prompt injection. Temperature affects randomness, not security. Authentication prevents unauthorized access but not injection, and fine-tuning on small datasets doesn’t address injection.

question_html: In the context of AI system monitoring, what does “prediction drift” track?

options.text: Changes in the distribution of the model’s predicted classes or scores over time

explanation_html: Prediction drift monitors how the model’s output distribution evolves, which can signal concept drift or data drift, even if input features appear stable. It helps detect silent model degradation.

question_html: A company wants to ensure its AI voice assistant only activates after a specific wake word and does not transmit private conversations to the cloud without consent. Which responsible AI principle is primarily at stake?
explanation_html: Unauthorized audio transmission violates user privacy and security principles. Ensuring data is only processed with consent and safeguarded is a core privacy requirement. Fairness, explainability, and robustness are less directly impacted.

question_html: What is the main purpose of rate limiting on an AI inference API?

options.text: To prevent abuse and ensure service availability under high load

explanation_html: Rate limiting restricts the number of requests a user can make in a given timeframe, protecting the service from DDoS attacks, excessive costs, and resource exhaustion, thus maintaining availability.

question_html: Which of the following is an example of a proactive AI security measure during model development?

options.text: Running static analysis on model serialization formats to detect vulnerable code

explanation_html: Proactive security includes scanning model files (e.g., Pickle, ONNX) for embedded malicious code or known vulnerabilities before deployment. Monitoring, rollback, and post-incident reviews are reactive or operational measures.

question_html: A team uses feature importance scores from a model-agnostic method to explain individual predictions to end users. Which technique is likely being applied?
explanation_html: SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) and LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations) provide local explanations for individual predictions. PCA and t-SNE are dimensionality reduction/visualization, and K-means is clustering.

question_html: In a continuous delivery pipeline for ML models, what does a “smoke test” typically verify before full production traffic is routed?

options.text: The model’s training accuracy on historical data
The deployed service can handle a few basic requests without crashing
The fairness metrics across all demographic slices

explanation_html: A smoke test is a quick sanity check that the newly deployed model service starts, responds correctly to simple inputs, and doesn’t error out. It’s a first-level gate before more thorough testing. Training accuracy, fairness, and carbon footprint are not part of this initial live check.

question_html: What is the primary reason to implement model versioning in a production environment?

options.text: To reduce the model file size
To enable traceability, rollback, and comparison of different model iterations

explanation_html: Model versioning assigns unique identifiers to each trained model artifact, allowing teams to track which version is in production, quickly roll back to a prior version, and compare performance across versions.

question_html: A large language model occasionally produces factually incorrect statements with high confidence. What is this phenomenon called?
explanation_html: Hallucination refers to the generation of plausible-sounding but incorrect or nonsensical information. Overfitting is a training issue where the model memorizes rather than generalizes; the others are unrelated to factual errors.

question_html: Which regulatory framework specifically requires that individuals have the right not to be subject to solely automated decisions that produce legal effects?
explanation_html: GDPR Article 22 provides the right to human intervention for decisions based solely on automated processing that have legal or similarly significant effects. HIPAA is health data privacy, PCI DSS is payment card security, and SOC 2 is a trust services framework.

question_html: What is the purpose of a feature store in an operational ML platform?

options.text: To store raw log files for debugging
To provide a centralized repository for consistent feature definitions and serving

explanation_html: A feature store ensures that the same feature engineering logic is used during training and inference, reducing training-serving skew and enabling feature reuse. It doesn’t store logs or manage containers.

question_html: A monitoring dashboard for a fraud detection model shows a sudden spike in false positive rate. What should be the first troubleshooting step?

options.text: Immediately retrain the model on all available data
Check for recent changes in data sources or transaction patterns
Reduce the number of serving replicas

explanation_html: A spike in false positives often indicates a change in input data or environment. Investigating data sources and recent pattern shifts helps identify root cause before taking action like retraining or adjusting infrastructure.

question_html: Which of the following is a best practice for managing credentials used by an AI service to access a backend database?

options.text: Hardcode credentials in the model’s source code
Store credentials in a secure secrets manager and rotate them regularly
Share a single set of credentials across all environments
Embed credentials in the container image

explanation_html: Using a secrets manager (like a vault) with automated rotation reduces the risk of credential leakage. Hardcoding, sharing, or embedding in images are security anti-patterns.

question_html: In an AI governance framework, what is the role of an impact assessment for a new AI use case?

options.text: To calculate the total cost of infrastructure
To identify potential ethical, legal, and societal risks before development
To measure model latency under load
To determine the optimal batch size for training

explanation_html: AI impact assessments (e.g., Data Protection Impact Assessment, Algorithmic Impact Assessment) evaluate risks to rights and freedoms, helping decide whether and how to proceed with the project responsibly.

question_html: A team wants to detect when a chatbot starts generating toxic language in real time. Which mechanism is most appropriate?

options.text: Post-hoc static analysis of logs after 24 hours
Real-time content moderation using a toxicity classifier
Manual review of all generated messages weekly

explanation_html: Real-time toxicity classifiers can intercept and block or flag harmful outputs instantly, preventing exposure to end users. Delayed analysis or manual review cannot prevent immediate harm.

question_html: An LLM system is designed to refuse answering harmful queries. An attacker uses a long, convoluted hypothetical story to eventually ask for dangerous instructions. What type of attack is this?

options.text: Prompt injection using role-playing and context manipulation

explanation_html: Attackers craft elaborate narratives to circumvent safety guardrails, which is a form of prompt injection exploiting the model’s context-following ability. Robust safety filters must detect intent, not just keywords.

question_html: In a responsible AI framework, what does “contestability” mean for end users?

options.text: Users can compete to improve the model's accuracy
Users have a clear mechanism to challenge or seek human review of automated decisions that affect them
Users can modify the model's training data
Users must accept all AI decisions without question

explanation_html: Contestability ensures that individuals can dispute AI-driven outcomes, request human intervention, and receive explanations, reinforcing accountability and user rights.

question_html: An AI model is deployed as a microservice. The operations team needs to detect a sudden increase in the rate of non-200 HTTP responses. Which metric type is most relevant?

options.text: Error rate on the inference endpoint

explanation_html: Monitoring the error rate (proportion of 4xx/5xx responses) directly signals operational issues with the service, such as overload, misconfiguration, or model failures.

question_html: Which of the following is an example of a content safety risk in a multi-modal AI system that processes both text and images?

options.text: The model generates a longer response than expected
The model outputs a description promoting violence after receiving a neutral image
The model uses too much GPU memory

explanation_html: Multi-modal models can produce harmful outputs based on visual inputs. Ensuring outputs across all modalities are safe is a core content safety requirement.

question_html: A team automates the training pipeline so that a new model version is only promoted if it shows a statistically significant improvement in accuracy on a holdout set. Which practice does this represent?
explanation_html: Evaluation gating integrates automatic performance checks into the deployment pipeline, blocking models that fail predefined criteria, thus maintaining quality.

question_html: A production AI system uses a shared database for multiple models. What is a key operational risk if one model overwhelms the database with requests?

options.text: Noisy neighbor effect leading to degraded performance for other models

explanation_html: In shared infrastructure, one component consuming excessive resources can starve others, a “noisy neighbor” problem. Resource isolation and throttling are necessary mitigations.

question_html: An AI auditor reviews a system and finds that the developers cannot reproduce a specific model version’s training results. What is missing?

options.text: Model reproducibility and adequate lineage tracking

explanation_html: Reproducibility requires versioned data, code, hyperparameters, and environment. Without it, debugging and compliance audits are severely hindered.

question_html: Which technique is designed to protect user privacy by applying mathematical transformations so that data remains usable for training while making re-identification difficult?
explanation_html: Differential privacy adds controlled noise, providing a formal privacy guarantee. It differs from encryption, which protects data storage but not against inference from model outputs.

question_html: A user reports receiving a loan denial decision based on an AI model, but the reason provided is “score below threshold.” Why does this lack meaningful explainability?

options.text: It does not convey the key factors that influenced the score, making the decision opaque

explanation_html: Meaningful explanations should reference influential features (e.g., “low income, high debt-to-income ratio”) to allow users to understand and potentially contest the outcome.

question_html: During model deployment, a canary instance shows a memory leak. What should happen according to a robust automated release process?

options.text: The canary is promoted to full production
The canary is rolled back and an alert is triggered, blocking the release
The memory leak is ignored if accuracy is high
The number of instances is doubled

explanation_html: Automated rollback on critical signals like memory leaks prevents unstable code from reaching users, maintaining service reliability.

question_html: What does a model’s “sensitivity” in a medical diagnosis AI refer to?

options.text: The proportion of healthy patients correctly identified
The proportion of actual patients with the disease correctly identified (true positive rate)
The overall accuracy of the model

explanation_html: Sensitivity (recall) focuses on catching as many true cases as possible, crucial in medical screening where missing a disease is dangerous.

question_html: An organization uses AI to screen job applications. To align with fairness principles, what must be done regarding protected characteristics (e.g., race, gender)?

options.text: Always use them as features for accuracy
Either exclude them or carefully monitor and mitigate any indirect bias through proxy variables

explanation_html: Using protected attributes directly is often illegal or unethical. Even without direct use, proxy variables can introduce bias; continuous monitoring and mitigation are required.

question_html: In monitoring, what does a “prediction distribution shift” directly indicate?

options.text: The model's output labels or probabilities are changing over time, possibly reflecting drift

explanation_html: Tracking the output distribution (e.g., class balance, score histograms) can reveal drift or a broken feature pipeline before accuracy metrics are available.

question_html: Which of the following is a recommended practice for handling API keys used by an AI service?

options.text: Commit them to the public repository
Rotate keys periodically and never hardcode them; use a secrets manager
Use the same key for all environments indefinitely

explanation_html: Secrets management with rotation minimizes the impact of a leaked key, while hardcoding and sharing are severe security anti-patterns.

question_html: A team wants to estimate the carbon footprint of their model inference in production. What should they primarily measure?

options.text: The number of lines of code
Energy consumption of the serving infrastructure and multiply by carbon intensity of the grid
The size of the training corpus

explanation_html: Operational carbon footprint is a function of energy used and the carbon per kilowatt-hour. This aligns with sustainability goals in AI operations.

question_html: A team deploys a model that uses a third-party pre-trained component. What is the primary security concern regarding the supply chain?

options.text: The possibility of hidden backdoors or vulnerabilities embedded in the pre-trained weights
The color of the component's logo
The number of layers in the component

explanation_html: Pre-trained models can contain malicious code or backdoors that execute when loaded. Supply chain security requires scanning and verifying the integrity of all external artifacts before deployment.

question_html: In a Kubernetes-based AI deployment, what is the function of a health probe?

options.text: To check if the container is running and ready to serve requests, restarting it if it fails

explanation_html: Liveness and readiness probes allow the orchestrator to automatically detect and recover from crashed or stuck containers, improving resilience.

question_html: A company must comply with HIPAA for a medical AI application. Which measure is essential?

options.text: Making all patient data publicly accessible
Implementing strong access controls, audit logs, and encrypting protected health information (PHI) in transit and at rest

explanation_html: HIPAA mandates safeguards for PHI. Access controls, audit trails, and encryption are fundamental technical requirements.

question_html: A data scientist adds a new feature to a model but forgets to update the inference pipeline’s feature generation code. What type of skew occurs?
explanation_html: When training and inference features are computed differently, the model receives unexpected inputs, causing severe accuracy loss. This is a training-serving skew.

question_html: What is the primary purpose of an AI risk register?

options.text: To list all models that have never failed
To document identified risks, their likelihood, impact, and mitigation strategies for each AI system
To track the daily stock price

explanation_html: A risk register is a governance tool for proactively managing AI risks (e.g., bias, security, operational), assigning ownership, and tracking controls.

question_html: A team uses a “shadow mode” deployment for a new fraud detection model. The new model’s alerts are not shown to analysts yet. What is the main limitation of this approach for evaluation?

options.text: It cannot measure false positive rate in a real-world setting
It cannot capture the downstream effects of actions taken based on the model's alerts

explanation_html: Shadow mode evaluates output quality but cannot measure business impact because humans don’t act on its predictions, so the feedback loop is missing.

question_html: In AI reliability engineering, what does “mean time to detect” (MTTD) measure?

options.text: The time to train a model
The average time taken to identify a production incident after it starts
The average latency of API calls

explanation_html: MTTD is a key incident response metric. Lower MTTD indicates effective monitoring and alerting, leading to faster recovery.

question_html: Which of the following is an example of a “representation harm” in AI?

options.text: The model denies a loan unfairly
A translation model associates "nurse" only with female pronouns, reinforcing stereotypes

explanation_html: Representational harm involves stereotypes, denigration, or erasure of groups in outputs. Allocative harm is about resource distribution (loan denial). Both are fairness concerns.

question_html: An organization’s AI policy requires that every high-risk model have a documented “exit strategy.” What does this entail?

options.text: A plan to sell the model
Procedures for decommissioning the model safely, including data handling and communication to affected users
A plan to increase training data indefinitely

explanation_html: An exit strategy covers termination of the AI service, ensuring data is properly disposed, users notified, and dependencies removed, all in a compliant manner.

question_html: A model serving system experiences “cold start” latency spikes. What does this mean?

options.text: The first request after a period of inactivity takes much longer because the model needs to be loaded into memory
The model generates cold, unfeeling responses
The server room temperature is low

explanation_html: Cold start occurs when an inference container or function has to initialize (load model weights, libraries) before serving, causing a one-time latency penalty. Mitigations include keeping instances warm.

question_html: Which evaluation metric directly measures how often a model’s top-5 predicted classes contain the true label for a multi-class image classifier?
explanation_html: Top-5 accuracy reflects whether the correct class is among the model’s five highest probability predictions, useful when perfect top-1 accuracy is difficult but narrowing to a few candidates is acceptable.

question_html: In a continuous monitoring setup, what does “data integrity” checking involve?

options.text: Validating that data has not been corrupted, tampered with, or altered in an unauthorized manner during transit or storage

explanation_html: Data integrity checks, such as checksums or audit hashes, ensure that the data used for inference is exactly as intended, preventing silent corruption or security breaches.

question_html: A model update introduces a bias against a protected group that was not present in the previous version. Which practice would have most likely caught this?

options.text: Running automated fairness metrics as part of the deployment pipeline and comparing against the previous baseline

explanation_html: Automated fairness regression testing in CI/CD compares new model metrics against the current production model, flagging unexpected degradations before release.

question_html: A company uses an external API for a content safety filter. The API experiences an outage. What should the AI system do according to responsible AI safety design?

options.text: Bypass the safety filter and serve all responses
Fail closed: either stop serving or return a safe default message until the filter is available
Serve the model's raw output without filtering

explanation_html: A fail-closed approach prioritizes safety over availability. Bypassing safety controls can lead to harmful outputs being served, violating responsible AI commitments.

question_html: What is the primary reason to use a “model card” even for an internal-only AI system?

options.text: To provide internal stakeholders and auditors with transparent documentation about the model's capabilities, limitations, and risks

explanation_html: Model cards serve as transparency artifacts that help internal governance, risk management, and ensure responsible use, not just external communication.

question_html: Which of the following is a common metric for evaluating the calibration of a probabilistic classifier?
explanation_html: ECE measures how well predicted probabilities align with actual empirical frequencies. Well-calibrated probabilities are important for risk-sensitive applications. MSE is for regression, others for clustering or distance.

question_html: A company uses personal data to train a model. Under GDPR, what must be provided to users regarding the processing of their data?

options.text: A vague statement that data may be used for undefined purposes
Clear, specific notice of data processing purposes and legal basis
A complex legal contract only in English
No information is required if the model is accurate

explanation_html: GDPR requires transparency through clear privacy notices detailing purposes, legal basis, retention, and rights. Vague or missing information is non-compliant.

question_html: In a responsible AI toolkit, what is the purpose of a fairness dashboard?

options.text: To compare model performance and error rates across sensitive demographic groups

explanation_html: Fairness dashboards allow stakeholders to interactively explore how model outcomes differ by group, helping identify and mitigate unfair biases. They are not for latency or key management.

question_html: Which attack involves inserting a malicious instruction into an image or text that causes an AI system to misinterpret the input?
explanation_html: Adversarial perturbations (in vision) or prompt injections (in language) exploit model vulnerabilities to change behavior or output. SQL injection and XSS target traditional web apps; man-in-the-middle intercepts communication.

question_html: What is the primary purpose of a service mesh in a microservices-based AI deployment?

options.text: To manage service-to-service communication, including traffic routing and security policies

explanation_html: A service mesh handles network connectivity, load balancing, retries, and mutual TLS between microservices without changing application code, enhancing reliability and security for AI components.

question_html: A model’s performance is stable, but the business impact of its errors has increased because the cost of a false negative has risen. What should be re-evaluated?

options.text: The decision threshold to balance precision and recall according to the new cost structure
The color of the monitoring dashboard

explanation_html: Changing error costs may warrant adjusting the classification threshold to favor higher recall (catching more positives) even if precision drops, aligning the model’s trade-offs with business risk.

question_html: Which of the following best describes “model lineage” in an MLOps platform?

options.text: A record of the model’s architecture, hyperparameters, training data, and code version used
The physical location of the model artifact
The list of users who called the model API

explanation_html: Model lineage tracks the metadata and artifacts that produced a specific model version, providing reproducibility and auditability. It’s crucial for debugging and compliance.

question_html: A team wants to ensure that a new NLP model does not leak sensitive training data through its outputs. What evaluation technique can help detect memorization?
explanation_html: By inserting unique canary sequences into the training data and testing if the model can regenerate them, teams can quantify unintended memorization. This is a direct privacy risk evaluation method.

question_html: What is the main advantage of using a semantic cache in an LLM inference service?

options.text: To reduce latency and cost by returning cached responses for semantically similar queries

explanation_html: A semantic cache stores previous query-response pairs and retrieves them when a new query is similar enough, avoiding costly re-inference. It improves efficiency and user experience.

question_html: In the context of AI incident response, what is the purpose of an after-action review (postmortem)?

options.text: To assign blame to a specific engineer
To learn from incidents without blame and improve processes and safeguards
To delete all logs related to the incident
To immediately retrain the model without analysis

explanation_html: A blameless postmortem focuses on understanding the root causes, systemic factors, and improving resilience, fostering a culture of reliability and safety in AI operations.

question_html: Which method helps validate that an AI system’s performance remains consistent after minor updates to its environment (e.g., library patches)?

options.text: Automated regression testing on a golden dataset

explanation_html: A golden dataset of curated inputs with known correct outputs can be run automatically as regression tests to catch any unexpected changes in model behavior after environment updates.

question_html: When designing an AI system that makes automated decisions with significant impact, what should be provided to the affected individuals according to responsible AI principles?

options.text: Meaningful information about the logic involved, significance, and envisaged consequences

explanation_html: Transparency and explainability require that individuals receive understandable information about how decisions are made, not raw data or irrelevant details, enabling them to contest or understand outcomes.

question_html: A model monitoring system tracks the percentage of inference requests resulting in a confidence score below 0.5. What does a sudden increase in this metric likely indicate?

options.text: The model has become more certain
Model uncertainty has increased, possibly due to data drift or new types of input
The serving hardware has been upgraded

explanation_html: A rise in low-confidence predictions suggests the model is encountering unfamiliar patterns, often a sign of data drift or domain shift, warranting further investigation.

question_html: What is the role of a data protection officer (DPO) in an organization deploying AI?
